core_themes.name: Productivity gap
core_themes.claim: Despite considerable economic strengths, Midlands productivity has fallen further behind the UK average (gap widening from about 10% to 15% between 1997 and 2015), with GVA per employee and business creation lagging.

core_themes.name: Skills shortage
core_themes.claim: The Midlands has a weaker skills base than other regions, with fewer highly qualified people, more with no qualifications, weaker school outcomes and poor graduate retention, which explains regional disparities in growth and productivity.

core_themes.name: Fragmented transport and connectivity
core_themes.claim: Slow, congested transport links within the region and a dispersed population fragment the economy, raising the cost of moving people, goods and ideas and lowering productivity and wages, despite good national and international links.

core_themes.name: Existing strengths to build on
core_themes.claim: The region has substantial assets (large economy, manufacturing and services base, industrial clusters, 20 universities, strong exports and inward investment) that provide a base for growth if the weaknesses are addressed.

core_themes.name: Local Growth Fund investment package
core_themes.claim: A £392 million Local Growth Fund allocation across the Midlands LEPs, funding specific local projects in transport, skills, clusters, housing and culture, will address barriers to productivity and help clusters grow.

core_themes.name: Connectivity measures
core_themes.claim: Investing in local transport upgrades, East-West links, smart ticketing, HS2 benefits and digital infrastructure will connect the region's towns and cities and to the rest of the country, addressing fragmentation and raising productivity.

core_themes.name: Midlands Skills Challenge
core_themes.claim: A £20 million Skills Challenge, with Work Coaches, English-language training, mental health pilots and lifelong learning trials, plus skills infrastructure investment, is the first step towards closing the skills gap.

core_themes.name: Enterprise, innovation, trade and investment
core_themes.claim: The Midlands Engine Investment Fund of over £250 million, support for science and innovation clusters, and a Trade and Investment Programme and Investment Portfolio will make the economy more dynamic and attract trade and investment.

proposal.note: The proposal is a package of many separate funded measures grouped under five objectives, with little argument for why each was chosen over alternatives.

core_themes.name: Delivery through local partnership
core_themes.claim: The government cannot deliver the strategy alone, so delivery relies on the Midlands Engine Partnership, combined authorities, LEPs, local authorities, universities and businesses, backed by £4 million of funding and an industry board.

core_themes.name: Delivery of connectivity and HS2 benefits
core_themes.claim: Connectivity measures will be delivered by working with Midlands Connect, Transport for West Midlands and local authorities around HS2 stations, with Midlands Connect on the national Smart Ticketing Delivery Board.

core_themes.name: Work still to be designed
core_themes.claim: Details of skills, innovation and productivity measures are to be developed jointly with partners, such as the long-term skills plan, innovation-ready proposals and supply chain programme, rather than fixed now.

core_themes.name: Trade and investment delivery timetable
core_themes.claim: The Trade and Investment Programme is delivered through a schedule of dated events, missions, summits and publications with local partners.

implementation.note: Implementation is mostly a list of partnership arrangements and activities, with no reasoning about why these delivery methods were chosen or alternatives considered.
